info.title: Crypto Pricing API
info.description:
Prices for crypto assets, served from a cache that a background worker keeps fresh. The API
**never calls the upstream data provider** on the request path.

## Authentication
Send your consumer key in the **`X-API-Key`** header (click **Authorize** above). Keys look like
`cp_live_...` and are created by an operator with `python -m app.cli create-key`.
`/v1/admin/*` uses a different key in **`X-Admin-Key`**; an admin key is never valid on consumer
endpoints and vice versa. Bad keys all return the same `401 invalid_api_key`. Repeated failures
from one IP are throttled with `429`.

## Rate limits
Every authenticated response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit` (requests per window),
`X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until a slot frees up). Over the limit
you get `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header (seconds).

## Conventions
- **Decimals.** `price`, `price_toman`, `volume_24h`, `market_cap`, `high_24h` and `low_24h` are JSON
  *strings* (exact decimals, never scientific notation). Percent changes are JSON numbers.
- **Sparkline.** Every price object has a chart-ready 7-day `sparkline`; pass `sparkline=false`
  to omit it. Point `i` is at `start + i * interval_seconds` (Unix seconds, UTC); `null` means no data
  (never forward-filled). The last point is the live price. The values are plain JSON **numbers**
  (the one exception to the decimal-string rule, because chart libraries need numbers).
  `source` is `history`, `percent_change_anchors` (day-one fallback) or `none`.
- **IRR** is the Iranian Rial; `price_toman` = Rial / 10.
- **Derived pairs.** A pair whose quote is not USD/BTC/ETH/IRR (e.g. `SOL/USDT`) is a cross rate
  computed as `base_usd / quote_usd` (`derived: true`). These are aggregated market rates,
  **not exchange order-book prices**.
- **Freshness.** `fetched_at`, `age_seconds` and `stale` are on every price.
- **Errors** always look like `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id"}}`.

get.description:
Standard `PriceItem`s (plus `pair_ref`) for many coins, from Postgres.

Search ranks an exact symbol match first, then symbol prefix, then name/slug prefix, then
anything containing the text, then by rank. Sorting puts missing values last in both
directions and breaks ties by rank, so pages are stable. Sparklines come from the Redis cache
only (a coin without a cached sparkline gets an all-null one with `coverage: 0`); this endpoint
never builds one from history and does not count towards hot-set promotion.

For `quote=IRR` only `search`, `rank_max` and `sort` in `rank | name | price` apply (the
upstream has no IRR volume, market cap or percent changes); anything else is a 422
`unsupported_for_quote`.

get.description:
Look up `BASE/QUOTE` pairs. Separators `/`, `-` and `_` are accepted and
matching is case-insensitive. BASE may be a symbol, a slug or `id:<cmc_id>`; a ticker shared
by several coins resolves to the best rank (the response echoes `base.id` / `base.slug`).

* `USD`, `BTC`, `ETH`, `IRR` quotes are **native** (`derived: false`).
* Any other coin as QUOTE is a **derived cross rate** (`derived: true`): `base_usd / quote_usd`.
  Derived pairs are aggregated market rates, **not exchange order-book prices**; their volume,
  market cap and 24h high/low are `null`. Disabled when `PAIRS_ALLOW_CROSS=false`.

A well-formed request always returns HTTP 200 with per-pair `errors` (`invalid_pair`,
`unknown_base`, `unknown_quote`, `same_base_quote`, `cross_disabled`, `no_data`). Results keep
request order with duplicates removed. 422: empty list, too many pairs or malformed body.

get.description:
History for custom ranges (the standard `sparkline` is the default chart data).

Stored quotes (`HISTORY_QUOTES`, default USD and IRR) are read directly; BTC/ETH-quoted
history is derived per bucket from USD history (`derived: true`). Each bucket holds the last
snapshot in it. Max range per interval is configurable.
